title: The AI Teacher Test: Measuring the Pedagogical Ability of Blender and GPT-3 in Educational Dialogues
task_or_dataset: dialogue context and student utterance -> alternative tutor response; 52 selected items
human_expert_role: real teacher responses as references; 120 crowd raters
rubric_or_metric: pairwise teacher-likeness, understanding and helpfulness; Bayesian Bradley-Terry scores
reliability_evidence: calibration-example agreement 95%, 83% and 86%; full-task coefficient not reported
main_findings: GPT-3 and Blender were below human teachers, especially on helpfulness.
limitations: small selected English sample; raters were not necessarily educators
relevance_to_project: supports separate contextual understanding and helpfulness criteria

title: MathDial: A Dialogue Tutoring Dataset with Rich Pedagogical Properties Grounded in Math Reasoning Problems
tutoring_capabilities: misconception diagnosis; probing; focus; scaffolding; self-correction
task_or_dataset: problem, solution, misconception and dialogue history -> next tutor turn
human_expert_role: 91 experienced teachers authored dialogues and selected moves
rubric_or_metric: coherence, correctness, equitable tutoring; Success@k and Telling@k
reliability_evidence: move agreement kappa=.60; criterion human-evaluation kappa=.29/.69/.34
main_findings: general LLMs often gave incorrect feedback or revealed solutions too early.
limitations: simulated students; English mathematics; several weak-agreement labels
relevance_to_project: direct support for diagnosis, scaffolding and answer-revelation flags
evidence_location: Table 1 p.5603; Table 2 p.5605; Sections 3.1-3.4; Table 5 p.5609

title: The BEA 2023 Shared Task on Generating AI Teacher Responses in Educational Dialogues
task_or_dataset: dialogue context and student turn -> next teacher response
human_expert_role: education/training raters judged top systems
rubric_or_metric: BERTScore, DialogRPT and pairwise teacher-likeness, understanding, helpfulness
reliability_evidence: three raters per pair; formal coefficient not reported
main_findings: generic automatic metrics were vulnerable to surface changes and could prefer answer-giving.
limitations: human evaluation only for top systems; truncated context
relevance_to_project: generic overlap/dialogue metrics should not be primary pedagogical scores

title: Bridge: A Dataset for Facilitating Mistake Correction in Human-AI Tutoring
tutoring_capabilities: error diagnosis; remediation strategy; pedagogical intention; feedback
task_or_dataset: five-turn history and mistake -> error, strategy, intention and revised response
human_expert_role: experts annotated errors, strategies, intentions and revised responses
rubric_or_metric: usefulness, care, humanness and preference on a five-point comparative scale
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: responses conditioned on expert decisions were preferred; random decisions reduced quality.
limitations: elementary mathematics; few US experts; some context omitted
relevance_to_project: supports separating diagnosis and response quality

title: Unifying AI Tutor Evaluation: An Evaluation Taxonomy for Pedagogical Ability Assessment of LLM-Powered AI Tutors
tutoring_capabilities: mistake identification/location; guidance; actionability; coherence; tone; answer revelation
task_or_dataset: 192 conversations and 1,596 tutor responses -> three-class labels on eight dimensions
human_expert_role: experts validated taxonomy, double-annotated and adjudicated gold labels
rubric_or_metric: eight three-level pedagogical criteria; Desired Annotation Match Rate
reliability_evidence: taxonomy Fleiss kappa=.65; production average Cohen kappa=.71
main_findings: strong answer-generation models were not consistently strong tutors; evaluator quality varied by dimension.
limitations: mathematics and mistake remediation; dimensions treated independently
relevance_to_project: strong source for analytic criterion vectors and teacher adjudication

title: MathTutorBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Open-ended Pedagogical Capabilities of LLM Tutors
tutoring_capabilities: solution verification; mistake correction; Socratic questioning; scaffolding; long-dialog maintenance
task_or_dataset: seven tasks with problem, student solution/history and optional intent
human_expert_role: source datasets use teachers and expert revisions; expert/novice responses validate reward model
rubric_or_metric: structured metrics plus learned scaffolding reward and win rate
reliability_evidence: reward model up to .84 accuracy distinguishing expert from novice on held-out Bridge data
main_findings: subject solving did not imply tutoring quality; general models degraded in longer dialogue.
limitations: learned metric is a proxy; mathematics only; no learning-gain inference
relevance_to_project: supports separate correctness, understanding and pedagogy plus a long-history subset

title: TutorBench: A Benchmark To Assess Tutoring Capabilities Of Large Language Models
tutoring_capabilities: adaptive explanation; feedback; active-learning hints; diagnosis
task_or_dataset: question, student work/history and optional image -> tutor response; 1,490 samples
human_expert_role: subject experts authored questions, golden responses and sample-specific rubrics
rubric_or_metric: 3-39 binary criteria per sample; critical and ordinary weights
reliability_evidence: mean inter-human agreement .75; LLM-human .78; judge F1=.82
main_findings: best evaluated model remained below 56%; sample-specific rubrics exposed capability gaps.
limitations: static prewritten contexts; full dataset not public at extraction time
relevance_to_project: supports sample-specific criteria and separate critical failures, not inherited weights

title: The BEA 2025 Shared Task on Pedagogical Ability Assessment of AI-Powered Tutors
task_or_dataset: dialogue and tutor response -> three-class dimension labels
human_expert_role: organizers annotated, double-annotated and adjudicated
rubric_or_metric: macro-F1 over MRBench taxonomy
reliability_evidence: Fleiss kappa=.65; organizer calibration kappa=.64 before resolution
main_findings: guidance remained particularly difficult for automatic systems.
limitations: short English mathematics contexts; limited tutor set
relevance_to_project: supports mandatory adjudication for ambiguous partial performance

title: Rethinking Scaffolding in LLM Tutors: The Role of Student Uptake
task_or_dataset: complete dialogues -> turn-level scaffolding and uptake scores
human_expert_role: metric validated against existing human-labelled data
rubric_or_metric: 1-5 scaffolding and student-uptake scores
reliability_evidence: judge accuracy 93.8% on a 550-chat human-labelled sample
main_findings: benchmark conversations had higher uptake than real deployments; students often redirected or bypassed scaffolding.
limitations: LLM judge; heterogeneous datasets; uptake is not learning gain
relevance_to_project: supports a distinct multi-turn uptake field and caution about static benchmarks
evidence_location: Sections 1 and 3; Table 1; results and discussion

title: The Missing Evaluation Axis: Measuring Student Uptake of Tutor Feedback in Programming
tutoring_capabilities: misconception feedback; relevance; immediate revision uptake
task_or_dataset: feedback plus consecutive code submissions -> pedagogy, relevance and success labels
human_expert_role: two humans annotated validation samples; student helpfulness supplied external signal
rubric_or_metric: MRBench dimensions plus relevance and success scores
reliability_evidence: human-human kappa=.76; LLM-human kappa=.65/.44
main_findings: uptake measures differentiated tutors beyond static pedagogy scores.
limitations: non-randomized; immediate uptake; undergraduate code
relevance_to_project: supports retaining next-revision evidence without treating it as learning gain

title: Automated Feedback Generation for Introductory Programming Assignments
task_or_dataset: 6,431 incorrect submissions with reference implementation and error model
human_expert_role: instructor provides reference implementation and correction rules
rubric_or_metric: repair coverage, runtime, number of corrections, feedback detail
reliability_evidence: not_applicable
main_findings: constraint-based matching repaired 64% of incorrect submissions.
limitations: manual rules and reference solution required; no learner evaluation
relevance_to_project: supports diagnosis/localization but not a claim of tutoring effectiveness

title: Data-Driven Hint Generation in Vast Solution Spaces: a Self-Improving Python Programming Tutor
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
task_or_dataset: canonicalized student program states in a solution-space graph
human_expert_role: teacher supplies tests, exemplar solutions and may adjust path weights
rubric_or_metric: graph coverage, hint availability and path quality
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: data-driven graphs produced incremental hints across multiple valid solutions.
limitations: technical evaluation; sparse-data and language-specific requirements
relevance_to_project: supports smallest useful next step and preservation of alternative algorithms

title: Adaptive Immediate Feedback Can Improve Novice Programming Engagement and Intention to Persist in Computer Science
task_or_dataset: programming assignments with or without adaptive feedback
human_expert_role: educators/researchers designed the intervention
rubric_or_metric: engagement, subsequent performance and intention to persist
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: adaptive feedback was associated with stronger engagement and persistence.
limitations: one environment and setting; detailed licensed-text audit incomplete
relevance_to_project: closest learner-level evidence for immediate programming feedback
evidence_location: Publisher abstract; Results and Discussion require follow-up

title: Exploring the Responses of Large Language Models to Beginner Programmers' Help Requests
tutoring_capabilities: explain errors; answer authentic help requests; guide next action
task_or_dataset: 150 authentic requests and 600 generated responses
human_expert_role: course teacher provided baseline responses; researchers categorized outputs
rubric_or_metric: seven binary aspects including correctness, relevance, explanation and solution provision
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: responses could be useful but also incorrect, overlong or overly solution-revealing.
limitations: one English course; single-turn; no learning outcomes
relevance_to_project: supports clarifying-question, relevance and leakage criteria

title: Generative AI for Programming Education: Benchmarking ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Human Tutors
tutoring_capabilities: issue identification; next-step hints; guided problem solving
task_or_dataset: 25 student programs and 150 human/model hints
human_expert_role: two experienced tutors authored and evaluated hints
rubric_or_metric: issue identification, guided problem solving, disclosure and readability
reliability_evidence: two evaluators; disagreements resolved; no coefficient
main_findings: GPT-4 approached tutors on issue identification/readability but lagged on guidance and concealment.
limitations: small dataset; English Python; same tutors authored and evaluated
relevance_to_project: strong direct source for algorithm construction and diagnosis criteria

title: Evaluating the Application of Large Language Models to Generate Feedback in Programming Education
task_or_dataset: 51 students and three programming assignments
human_expert_role: course staff supplied tasks, tests and solution context
rubric_or_metric: issue coverage, false issues, acceptance and usefulness
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: accepted feedback could still be incomplete; perceived usefulness did not equal correctness.
limitations: one institution/model; few manually evaluated tasks
relevance_to_project: supports separating issue coverage, false positives and perceived usefulness

title: Not the Silver Bullet: LLM-enhanced Programming Error Messages are Ineffective in Practice
task_or_dataset: 106 participants and six seeded syntax errors
human_expert_role: human-enhanced messages authored by researcher; experiment designed by educators
rubric_or_metric: correction time, skip rate and ratings
reliability_evidence: objective outcomes; no annotation reliability applicable
main_findings: LLM-enhanced messages did not improve correction time or skip rate; human messages helped some errors.
limitations: remote artificial task; one language and compiler
relevance_to_project: warns that fluent/long feedback is not a proxy for effective next action

title: Decoding Logic Errors: A Comparative Study on Bug Detection by Students and Large Language Models
task_or_dataset: 964 students, correct code and seeded logic errors; 360 LLM requests
human_expert_role: instructors authored variants and evaluated responses
rubric_or_metric: bug detection, false positives and response analysis
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: models often found intended bugs but also reported non-existent problems in correct code.
limitations: small snippets and single intended bugs; not dialogue tutoring
relevance_to_project: supports correct-work negative controls and false-positive critical failure

title: The TalkMoves Dataset: K-12 Mathematics Lesson Transcripts Annotated for Teacher and Student Discursive Moves
tutoring_capabilities: eliciting reasoning; pressing for accuracy; revoicing; relating ideas
task_or_dataset: 567 transcripts and ten mutually exclusive talk moves
human_expert_role: experts designed protocol; trained annotators double-coded and recalibrated
rubric_or_metric: six teacher and four student talk-move labels
reliability_evidence: per-label Cohen kappa .91-1.00 at initial/midpoint checks
main_findings: behavior-specific labels can be highly reliable with definitions and recalibration.
limitations: whole-class mathematics; rare-label imbalance
relevance_to_project: supports per-criterion training, double-coding and midpoint calibration

title: Towards Responsible Development of Generative AI for Education: An Evaluation-Driven Approach
tutoring_capabilities: engagement; guided discovery; mistake recognition; adaptation; accuracy
task_or_dataset: seven human and automatic evaluations of LearnLM-Tutor
human_expert_role: teachers and learners co-designed principles; pedagogical experts rated turns/conversations
rubric_or_metric: nine turn dimensions, conversation rubric, pairwise preferences and automatic critics
reliability_evidence: per-dimension Krippendorff alpha approximately -.038 to .663
main_findings: reliability differed widely by construct; automatic measures captured only some human signals.
limitations: English/WEIRD contexts; limited samples; no Vietnamese validation
relevance_to_project: supports analytic vectors, N/A, multiple raters and per-dimension reliability

title: ConvoLearn: A Teacher-Authored Dataset for Pedagogical Dialogue
tutoring_capabilities: cognitive engagement; formative assessment; accountability; agency
task_or_dataset: 2,134 teacher-authored dialogues; 1,250 high-quality subset
human_expert_role: 323 certified teachers authored; 31 independent teachers rated
rubric_or_metric: six dimensions/21 subdimensions and 1-5 effectiveness ratings
reliability_evidence: human-evaluation IRR not reported; silver labels used LLM adjudication
main_findings: teacher ratings supported targeted fine-tuning as proof of concept.
limitations: one English subject; simulated students; LLM annotation circularity
relevance_to_project: closest age evidence but requires cross-domain teacher validation
evidence_location: Sections 3-7; Tables 1-3; Appendices G and M

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
task_or_dataset: MT-Bench and large-scale human preference conversations
human_expert_role: expert/crowd preference labels provide comparison target
rubric_or_metric: pairwise and scalar LLM judgments
reliability_evidence: strong judges exceeded 80% agreement in this setting
main_findings: LLM judges approximate preferences but have position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases.
limitations: general chat preference does not establish pedagogical validity
relevance_to_project: supports only calibrated auxiliary judging with human oversight

title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
task_or_dataset: order-swapped response pairs
human_expert_role: authors manually labelled outcomes; human escalation proposed
rubric_or_metric: balanced-position calibration and entropy
reliability_evidence: human alignment reported; annotator IRR not reported
main_findings: response order could reverse model rankings.
limitations: small general benchmark and model set
relevance_to_project: requires order swapping/randomization and human review of unstable cases

title: Large Language Models are Inconsistent and Biased Evaluators
task_or_dataset: SummEval and RoSE responses under repeated prompts
human_expert_role: existing expert judgments used as reference
rubric_or_metric: rating distributions, repeated samples and prompt perturbations
reliability_evidence: low inter-sample agreement and prompt sensitivity
main_findings: judges showed familiarity, anchoring and prompt-wording instability.
limitations: summarization rather than tutoring; model versions evolve
relevance_to_project: supports frozen prompts, repeated runs and human calibration

title: MM-Eval: A Multilingual Meta-Evaluation Benchmark for LLM-as-a-Judge and Reward Models
task_or_dataset: five core subsets across 18 languages plus consistency across 122 languages
human_expert_role: human annotation details require further verification
rubric_or_metric: pairwise ranking accuracy and absolute-score consistency/fairness
reliability_evidence: cross-language correlation and fairness analyses
main_findings: English-strong evaluators degrade and become less fair in lower-resource languages.
limitations: work in progress; Vietnamese inclusion not confirmed in audit
relevance_to_project: Vietnamese judge validity must be tested directly

title: M3Exam: A Multilingual, Multimodal, Multilevel Benchmark for Examining Large Language Models
task_or_dataset: 12,317 questions in nine languages; about 23% image-dependent
human_expert_role: questions sourced from real official examinations
rubric_or_metric: answer accuracy
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: models struggled more in lower-resource/non-Latin languages and multimodal questions.
limitations: solving benchmark, not tutoring
relevance_to_project: supports language- and level-specific testing, not tutoring rubric dimensions

title: VNHSGE: Vietnamese High School Graduation Examination Benchmark
task_or_dataset: over 19,000 multiple-choice questions and 300 literature essays
human_expert_role: official/comparable exam materials; no tutor-response annotation
rubric_or_metric: accuracy and generated-answer comparison
reliability_evidence: not_reported
main_findings: models showed uneven Vietnamese performance, especially in mathematics and sciences.
limitations: Grade 12; no Informatics tutoring dialogue
relevance_to_project: direct Vietnamese precedent only for localization and content testing

title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
tutoring_capabilities: guiding questions; real-time tutor support; avoiding answer giving
task_or_dataset: 900 tutors and 1,800 students; more than 550,000 messages
human_expert_role: human tutors used AI suggestions; interviews and pedagogical classifiers evaluated practice
rubric_or_metric: topic mastery and pedagogical-strategy classifiers
reliability_evidence: preregistered RCT; classifier reliability must be checked in full text
main_findings: access increased topic mastery by 4 percentage points overall and changed tutor strategies.
limitations: human-AI copilot rather than autonomous tutor; mathematics context
relevance_to_project: supports teacher-in-the-loop design and answer-concealment behavior
